Training Load estimation vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Training Load support on Apple Watch covers storefront language. watchOS, HealthKit, and App Store Connect actually separate on-device training load estimation from product-page copy:

  • watchOS Training Load estimation — multi-day fitness strain calculated from workout history on supported Apple Watch models. Controls runtime Training Load cards, 7-day and 28-day trend charts, and recovery readiness readouts — not App Store language. AppLocale does not implement this.
  • HealthKit training load sample types — authorization, read queries, and Health history views for training load data. Your listing may mention Health Training Load history; wiring HealthKit queries is engineering, not listing copy.
  • In-app Training Load dashboards & recovery UI — training load graphs, recovery readiness cards, overreaching alert badges, and 训练负荷 settings enrollment in your app. Listing copy markets those surfaces on the product page; SwiftUI chart code is separate.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Training Load support in the binary.

Working Training Load on Apple Watch and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe training load, multi-day fitness strain, recovery readiness, and workout load accumulation on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement watchOS Training Load estimation or HealthKit sample queries.
